plainEnglishInsights: Usage: GA4 property 497892271 shows 5,614 active users for Jul 31-Aug 6, 2026, up 11.7% from the previous 7 days. Sessions rose 23.2% and total engaged hours rose 11.6%.

Engagement quality: average time per user held at about 72.1 minutes, which remains far above the original 12-minute success benchmark, even though engagement rate moved -11.5 percentage points versus the prior week.

TVOD: DotStudios shows $4,089.99 in seven-day TVOD sales across 195 paid transactions. The Ark family accounts for $2,276.90 (55.7% of paid net) and The Librarians family accounts for $1,803.10 (44.1%).

Sales reconciliation: DotStudios is now the best title/platform sales view for the week and includes web, Apple, Roku, Android, and Fire-platform purchases. Stripe ($1,426.31) and Apple ($1,406.32) are preserved as separate source checks and should not be added on top of DotStudios.
Apple: the latest manual App Store Connect snapshot shows $1,406.32 gross sales, 388 downloads, 69 in-app units, and 457 total units for Jul 31-Aug 6.
Roku: the Aug 7 App Engagement report shows 437 new installs, 485 average daily viewers, and 4,054 hours streamed. Roku App Engagement remains separate from GA4.

Paid acquisition: measurement needs repair before we can judge paid growth this week. Google Ads failed because the connector is calling deprecated API version v21, Meta remains stale from the last Nathan/Forge One Meta-only email, and paid-campaign impressions must remain separate from ElectricNOW in-app ad impressions.

Next tests: keep leaning into The Ark and The Librarians demand, test separate Facebook purchase campaigns by title in the strongest states, split iOS/Android budgets, refresh creative around season availability, and verify install-to-viewing quality before materially scaling spend.

metaAdsSummary.plainEnglish: Meta's latest report (Jul 5-11, 2026) shows the campaign PAUSED: $0.00 spend (down 100%), 0 impressions, 0 link clicks and 0 app installs, with 'No campaign metrics found for this period'. The prior report (Jul 2-8, 2026) was $40.80 spend / 2,539 impressions / 251 link clicks / 23 iOS installs at $1.77 each. Per PC Social Media (Nathan), ElectricNow is deliberately pivoting AWAY from Meta Ads to Roku Ads: mobile iOS/Android install retention was too low to justify spend, TV (Roku) is judged the most valuable audience, and DotStudio is setting up Roku conversion tracking. So the Meta drop to $0 is an intentional strategy change, not a reporting gap.
metaAdsSummary.paidAcquisitionInterpretation: PAID ACQUISITION ASSESSMENT (Meta, Jul 5-11, 2026). Meta paid acquisition is effectively OFF this week: spend $0.00 (-100%), 0 impressions and 0 iOS installs. This is an INTENTIONAL pivot away from Meta Ads toward Roku Ads (PC Social Media / Nathan): mobile retention was too low, TV is the priority audience, and Roku conversion tracking is being set up by DotStudio. Google Ads also had no spend this week (connector returned no rows for Jul 6-12). NET: essentially no paid acquisition ran this week on either Meta or Google. Effect on the platform: GA4 property-wide traffic eased (sessions 9,971 vs 10,320, about -3.4%; new users 1,179 vs 1,519) and week-unique active users are estimated lower (~3,800 vs 4,158) - consistent with paid acquisition being switched off, though week-to-week noise also contributes. We still do NOT claim true ROAS (no install->activation->sale join; installs are free, not paid sales). Distinguish paid-campaign impressions (0 Meta this week) from in-app ad impressions (GA4 ads_impression, last instrumented at 34,940 for Jun 29-Jul 5) - different things. NEXT TESTS: (1) stand up Roku Ads conversion tracking and measure install->first-play activation; (2) compare Roku Ads cost-per-install to the paused Meta baseline ($1.77 iOS); (3) confirm whether the traffic dip persists once Roku Ads spend begins.
metaAdsSummary.downloadGrainNote: Meta bought 0 app installs this week (campaign paused). Paid acquisition, when active, buys FREE app installs, not paid sales; installs are a distinct grain from visible platform sales and from in-app ad impressions.
metaAdsSummary.strategyNote: PC Social Media (Nathan) is pivoting ElectricNow from Meta Ads to Roku Ads due to low mobile iOS/Android retention; TV is the priority audience and DotStudio is configuring Roku conversion tracking. Meta $0 for Jul 5-11 reflects this deliberate pause.

plainEnglishSummary.overview: The strongest news this week is TVOD momentum: the latest DotStudios export shows $4,089.99 from 195 paid transactions for Jul 31-Aug 6, led by The Ark and The Librarians, while measured GA4 platform usage also grew week-over-week.
bullets: TVOD: DotStudios shows $4,089.99 in seven-day TVOD sales across 195 paid transactions. The Ark family accounts for $2,276.90 (55.7% of paid net) and The Librarians family accounts for $1,803.10 (44.1%).

Engagement quality: average time per user held at about 72.1 minutes, which remains far above the original 12-minute success benchmark, even though engagement rate moved -11.5 percentage points versus the prior week.

TVOD: DotStudios shows $4,089.99 in seven-day TVOD sales across 195 paid transactions. The Ark family accounts for $2,276.90 (55.7% of paid net) and The Librarians family accounts for $1,803.10 (44.1%).

Sales reconciliation: DotStudios is now the best title/platform sales view for the week and includes web, Apple, Roku, Android, and Fire-platform purchases. Stripe ($1,426.31) and Apple ($1,406.32) are preserved as separate source checks and should not be added on top of DotStudios.
Apple: the latest manual App Store Connect snapshot shows $1,406.32 gross sales, 388 downloads, 69 in-app units, and 457 total units for Jul 31-Aug 6.
Roku: the Aug 7 App Engagement report shows 437 new installs, 485 average daily viewers, and 4,054 hours streamed. Roku App Engagement remains separate from GA4.

Paid acquisition: measurement needs repair before we can judge paid growth this week. Google Ads failed because the connector is calling deprecated API version v21, Meta remains stale from the last Nathan/Forge One Meta-only email, and paid-campaign impressions must remain separate from ElectricNOW in-app ad impressions.

Next tests: keep leaning into The Ark and The Librarians demand, test separate Facebook purchase campaigns by title in the strongest states, split iOS/Android budgets, refresh creative around season availability, and verify install-to-viewing quality before materially scaling spend.
plainEnglishSummary.paidAcquisitionAssessment: Verdict: momentum is promising, but paid acquisition is not fully measurable this run. The platform and TVOD signals are positive; Google Ads/Meta reporting must be fixed or refreshed before claiming paid ads are driving the sales and viewing lift.
